description: This topic covers how to use relative pronouns and relative adverbs to form defining and non-defining relative clauses, including correct punctuation, the choice between who/whom and which/that, omitting the relative pronoun, and combining sentences.

mcq.questionText: Which relative pronoun is used to refer to people as the subject of a relative clause?

options.text: which
who
whose
where

mcq.explanation: 'Who' is the relative pronoun used for people when they act as the subject of the relative clause, e.g. 'the man who called'.

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence: 'This is the book _____ I borrowed from the library.'

options.text: who
whose
which
when

mcq.explanation: 'Which' (or 'that') refers to things; a book is a thing, so 'which' is correct. 'Who' and 'whose' refer to people.

options.text: whom
that
whose
which

mcq.explanation: 'Whose' is the possessive relative pronoun, e.g. 'the girl whose bag was stolen'.

mcq.questionText: Identify the relative clause in: 'The teacher who teaches us English is from Mwanza.'

options.text: The teacher
who teaches us English
is from Mwanza
from Mwanza

mcq.explanation: A relative clause begins with a relative pronoun and gives more information about a noun. 'Who teaches us English' describes 'the teacher'.

mcq.questionText: Which sentence contains a NON-defining relative clause?

options.text: The student who won the prize is my friend.
Mr. Juma, who teaches us Biology, is very kind.
The pen that I lost was new.
People who smoke risk their health.

mcq.explanation: A non-defining clause gives extra, non-essential information and is set off with commas. 'Mr. Juma' is already identified, so the clause is extra information.

mcq.questionText: In which sentence can 'that' correctly replace the relative pronoun?

options.text: My uncle, who lives in Dodoma, is a doctor.
The phone which I bought is excellent.
Dar es Salaam, which is a busy city, is hot.
My mother, whom I love, is a nurse.

mcq.explanation: 'That' can be used in defining relative clauses without commas. It cannot be used in non-defining clauses (those with commas).

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct option: 'The man _____ I met yesterday is a lawyer.'

options.text: which
whose
whom
where

mcq.explanation: 'Whom' is used for a person who is the object of the verb. Here the man is the object of 'met' ('I met the man'), so 'whom' is correct.

mcq.questionText: Which relative adverb correctly fills the gap: 'This is the village _____ I was born.'?

options.text: when
where
why
which

mcq.explanation: 'Where' is the relative adverb used to refer to a place, e.g. 'the village where I was born'.

mcq.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses commas for a non-defining relative clause?

options.text: My sister who lives abroad sent me a gift.
My sister, who lives abroad, sent me a gift.
My sister, who lives abroad sent me a gift.
My sister who lives abroad, sent me a gift.

mcq.explanation: A non-defining clause must be enclosed by a comma on both sides. The extra information 'who lives abroad' is set off by two commas.

mcq.questionText: In which sentence can the relative pronoun be omitted?

options.text: The girl who sings well is my cousin.
The book that is on the table is mine.
The film that we watched was boring.
The boy who broke the window ran away.

mcq.explanation: A relative pronoun can be omitted when it is the object of the clause, as in 'The film we watched...'. It cannot be omitted when it is the subject.

mcq.questionText: Combine correctly: 'The house is big. We bought the house.'

options.text: The house who we bought is big.
The house which we bought is big.
The house whose we bought is big.
The house where we bought is big.

mcq.explanation: The house is a thing and the object of 'bought', so 'which' (or 'that') joins the sentences: 'The house which we bought is big.'

options.text: Students, who fail the test, must repeat it.
Students who fail the test must repeat it.
Students who, fail the test must repeat it.
Students who fail the test, must repeat it.

mcq.explanation: 'Who fail the test' is a defining clause that identifies which students; defining clauses take no commas.

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct relative pronoun: 'The student _____ phone rang during the exam was punished.'

options.text: who
whom
whose
which

mcq.explanation: The phone belongs to the student, so the possessive 'whose' is required: 'the student whose phone rang'.

mcq.questionText: Which relative adverb best fits: 'I remember the day _____ we first met.'?

options.text: where
when
why
whose

mcq.explanation: 'When' is the relative adverb used to refer to a time, e.g. 'the day when we met'.

mcq.questionText: Which of these is a common ERROR in relative clauses?

options.text: Using 'who' for people
Using 'which' for things
Using 'that' after a comma in a non-defining clause
Using 'whose' to show possession

mcq.explanation: 'That' cannot be used in non-defining (comma) clauses; only 'who', 'whom', or 'which' may follow a comma. The other options are correct usages.

fib.questionText: The woman _____ won the election is a teacher. (relative pronoun for a person as subject)
fib.explanation: 'Who' is used for a person who is the subject of the relative clause.

fib.questionText: The car _____ I drive is very old. (relative pronoun for a thing)
fib.explanation: 'Which' (or 'that') refers to things such as a car.

fib.questionText: That is the boy _____ bicycle was stolen. (possessive relative pronoun)
fib.explanation: 'Whose' shows possession; the bicycle belongs to the boy.

fib.questionText: This is the school _____ I studied as a child. (relative adverb for place)
fib.explanation: 'Where' is the relative adverb used for a place.

fib.questionText: Sunday is the day _____ I rest. (relative adverb for time)
fib.explanation: 'When' is the relative adverb used for a time.

fib.questionText: Tell me the reason _____ you were late. (relative adverb for reason)
fib.explanation: 'Why' is the relative adverb used after 'reason' to give an explanation.

fib.questionText: The candidate _____ the voters trusted won easily. (formal relative pronoun for a person used as the object — begins with 'wh')
fib.explanation: 'Whom' is used for a person who is the object of the verb; here the candidate is the object of 'trusted'.

fib.questionText: A non-defining relative clause must be separated from the rest of the sentence by _____. (punctuation mark)
fib.explanation: Non-defining clauses give extra information and are enclosed by commas.

fib.questionText: The relative pronoun '_____' cannot be used in a non-defining clause after a comma. (one word)
fib.explanation: 'That' is used only in defining clauses; it cannot follow a comma in a non-defining clause.

fib.questionText: Combine using a relative pronoun: 'I know a man. The man speaks five languages.' Answer: I know a man _____ speaks five languages.
fib.explanation: The man is a person and the subject of 'speaks', so 'who' joins the sentences.

tf.questionText: 'Who' is used to refer to people in a relative clause.
tf.explanation: 'Who' refers to people, especially when they are the subject of the clause.

tf.questionText: 'Which' is used to refer to people.
tf.explanation: 'Which' refers to things or animals, not people. People take 'who' or 'whom'.

tf.questionText: Non-defining relative clauses are set off with commas.
tf.explanation: Non-defining clauses give extra information and are enclosed by commas.

tf.questionText: 'That' can be used in a non-defining relative clause after a comma.
tf.explanation: 'That' is only used in defining clauses. Non-defining clauses use 'who', 'whom', or 'which'.

tf.questionText: A defining relative clause gives essential information that identifies the noun.
tf.explanation: Defining (restrictive) clauses are essential to the meaning and identify which noun is meant; they take no commas.

tf.questionText: The relative pronoun can be omitted when it is the subject of the clause.
tf.explanation: It can be omitted only when it is the object, not the subject, of the clause.

tf.questionText: 'Whose' shows possession in a relative clause.
tf.explanation: 'Whose' is the possessive relative pronoun, e.g. 'the girl whose pen broke'.

tf.questionText: 'Where' is a relative adverb used to refer to time.
tf.explanation: 'Where' refers to place; 'when' refers to time.

tf.questionText: 'Whom' is used for a person who is the object of the verb in the relative clause.
tf.explanation: 'Whom' is the object form, as in 'the man whom I saw'.

tf.questionText: In the sentence 'My father, who is a farmer, is hardworking', removing the relative clause changes which father is meant.
tf.explanation: This is a non-defining clause giving extra information; removing it does not change which father is meant because 'my father' is already identified.

summary.correctAnswer: A clause that begins with a relative pronoun or adverb and gives more information about a noun.
summary.explanation: Relative clauses describe or identify nouns and are introduced by words like who, which, that, where, when, and why.

summary.questionText: List the five main relative pronouns.
summary.explanation: These five pronouns introduce relative clauses referring to people and things.
Relative adverbs introduce clauses about place (where), time (when), and reason (why).

summary.questionText: What is the difference between defining and non-defining relative clauses?
summary.correctAnswer: A defining clause gives essential information and uses no commas; a non-defining clause gives extra information and uses commas.
summary.explanation: Defining clauses identify the noun; non-defining clauses add removable extra detail and are punctuated with commas.

summary.questionText: When can 'that' NOT be used as a relative pronoun?
summary.explanation: 'That' is only used in defining clauses; non-defining clauses use who, whom, or which.

summary.questionText: When can a relative pronoun be omitted?
summary.correctAnswer: When it is the object of the relative clause.
summary.explanation: An object relative pronoun can be dropped, forming a contact clause, e.g. 'the book (which) I read'.

summary.questionText: Which relative pronoun is used to show possession?
summary.explanation: 'Whose' indicates that something belongs to the noun, e.g. 'the man whose car broke down'.

summary.questionText: What is the difference between 'who' and 'whom'?
summary.correctAnswer: 'Who' is the subject form and 'whom' is the object form.
summary.explanation: Use 'who' when the person does the action and 'whom' when the person receives the action.

summary.questionText: How do you combine two sentences using a relative clause?
summary.correctAnswer: Replace the repeated noun in the second sentence with a relative pronoun and join it to the noun in the first sentence.
summary.explanation: For example, 'The boy is my friend. The boy won' becomes 'The boy who won is my friend.'

summary.questionText: State one common error learners make with relative clauses.
summary.correctAnswer: Using 'that' in a non-defining clause, or using 'which' for people.
summary.explanation: These are frequent mistakes; people take who/whom and non-defining clauses cannot use 'that'.

hoq.questionText: Choose the sentence that combines 'The journalist reported the story. Everyone believed the journalist.' correctly using 'whom'.

options.text: The journalist who everyone believed reported the story.
The journalist whom everyone believed reported the story.
The journalist whose everyone believed reported the story.
The journalist which everyone believed reported the story.

hoq.explanation: The journalist is the object of 'believed' (everyone believed the journalist), so the object pronoun 'whom' is correct in formal usage.

hoq.questionText: Which sentence is BOTH grammatically correct AND correctly punctuated?

options.text: Kilimanjaro that is the highest mountain in Africa, attracts many climbers.
Kilimanjaro, which is the highest mountain in Africa, attracts many climbers.
Kilimanjaro which is the highest mountain in Africa attracts many climbers.
Kilimanjaro, that is the highest mountain in Africa, attracts many climbers.

hoq.explanation: Kilimanjaro is already identified, so the clause is non-defining and needs commas plus 'which' (not 'that'). Only option B uses both correctly.

hoq.questionText: In which sentence is the relative pronoun WRONGLY omitted?

options.text: The mango I ate was sweet.
The letter she wrote was long.
The dog bit the child was angry.
The song we heard was beautiful.

hoq.explanation: In option C the relative pronoun is the subject ('the dog that bit the child'), so it cannot be omitted. In the others the omitted pronoun is the object, which is allowed.
